other_leads: Paste checklist for https://business.adobe.com/blog/adobe-experience-manager-journey-optimizer-claude-design (blocked to automated tools): (1) the sentence "Adobe Experience Manager and Adobe Journey Optimizer are now available as workflow destinations" word for word; (2) for AEM: which AEM (AEM Sites as a Cloud Service, Edge Delivery Services and Experience Workspace, or both), that the page arrives for an author to review, and whether publishing is a separate step; (3) for Journey Optimizer: email only, that it becomes an editable content template, and whether it goes through Journey Optimizer's connector for Claude; (4) what the client needs first (Claude plan, Adobe sign-in, connector, admin approval, product roles); (5) any release words (available, beta, preview, coming).

Manual route, not a connector and not specific to Claude: Journey Optimizer imports an HTML file or a .zip folder into its Email Designer, then converts it so it can be edited and personalized (Experience League, updated November 18, 2026: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/journey-optimizer/using/channels/email/design-email/start-creating-content/existing-content, saved as pages/435d1bd80067.html). An HTML email from any design tool can come in this way.

If the paste says the AEM hand-off lands in Experience Workspace, the line goes to AEM Sites with Edge Delivery Services. Adobe describes Experience Workspace as the default for new Edge Delivery projects and the place where content made by agents and AI tools is reviewed, approved and deployed (Experience League Edge Delivery overview, updated November 11, 2026).

The AI registry's import-tool text can only count if the same words appear on a developer.adobe.com page. Today the registry loads its server data from ai.adobe.io and its documents from GitHub, and developer.adobe.com's sitemap (10,287 pages) has no page for the Journey Optimizer connector. A person could open https://developer.adobe.com/ai-registry/ in a browser to see what it shows, but the data there is still not an evidence page.
Journey Optimizer's 2026 release notes list a Coworker skill named Build Email from Figma (September 24, 2026). That is Figma, not Claude, and may matter to the Figma box.
AEM's Experience Modernization Agent (Experience League, November 12, 2026) takes Figma designs and supplied design references for redesigns. It does not name Claude Design.

The newsroom's June 18, 2026 release (the same day as the business.adobe.com post, per ChatGPT) covers Adobe's creative tools in ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini and Slack. It does not mention Claude Design, AEM or Journey Optimizer. The June 22 Cannes release says Adobe CX skills and MCP servers are generally available in Claude Enterprise, but names no Claude Design route.
